title: BACE: Applied Mathematics - BACE - Applied Mathematics - Dilutions
subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: You are provided with a **50X** stock solution of TAE buffer. You need to prepare **1000 mL** of **1X** TAE buffer. How much stock solution and water do you need?
questions.explain: Use $$C_1V_1 = C_2V_2$$: $$(50X)(V_1) = (1X)(1000 \text{ mL})$$. Solve for $V_1$: $$V_1 = \frac{1000}{50} = 20 \text{ mL}$$. To find the volume of water, subtract the stock volume from the total volume: $$1000 \text{ mL} - 20 \text{ mL} = 980 \text{ mL}$$.
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: What is the **dilution factor** if you add **0.1 mL** of sample to **9.9 mL** of diluent?
questions.explain: Dilution Factor (DF) = Total Volume / Sample Volume. $$\text{Total Volume} = 0.1 \text{ mL (sample)} + 9.9 \text{ mL (diluent)} = 10.0 \text{ mL}$$ ​$$\text{DF} = \frac{10.0}{0.1} = 100$$ This corresponds to a **1:100** dilution.
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: You perform a serial dilution: Tube 1 contains pure stock. Tube 2 is a 1:10 dilution of Tube 1. Tube 3 is a 1:10 dilution of Tube 2. What is the total dilution factor of **Tube 3** relative to the stock?
questions.explain: In serial dilutions, multiply the dilution factors of each step. $$\text{DF}_{total} = \text{DF}_1 \times \text{DF}_2 = 10 \times 10 = 100$$ The ratio is **1:100**.
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: You need a final concentration of **5 $\mu$g/mL** of a drug in a cell culture plate well holding **2 mL** of media. Your stock drug concentration is **1 mg/mL**. What volume of stock do you add to the well?
questions.explain:
1. Convert units to match. Stock = $1 \text{ mg/mL} = 1000 \text{ } \mu\text{g/mL}$.
2. Use $C_1V_1 = C_2V_2$: $$(1000 \text{ } \mu\text{g/mL})(V_1) = (5 \text{ } \mu\text{g/mL})(2 \text{ mL})$$
3. Solve: $$1000 V_1 = 10 \rightarrow V_1 = 0.01 \text{ mL}$$ 4. Convert to $\mu$L: $$0.01 \text{ mL} = 10 \text{ } \mu\text{L}$$
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: A technician adds **50 $\mu$L** of sample to **200 $\mu$L** of diluent. What is the dilution factor?
questions.explain: Total Volume = $50 + 200 = 250 \text{ } \mu\text{L}$. Dilution Factor = $\frac{\text{Total Vol}}{\text{Sample Vol}} = \frac{250}{50} = 5$. The dilution is **1:5** (1 part sample in 5 parts total).
